title: AWS WAF, Shield & Firewall Manager
summary: Layer 7 filtering, DDoS protection and central firewall policy across accounts.
tldr: **AWS WAF** filters HTTP(S) at layer 7 on CloudFront, ALB, API Gateway, AppSync, Cognito user pools and a few others. Use managed rule groups for SQLi/XSS, bots and account takeover.
**Shield Standard** is free and automatic against common L3/L4 attacks. **Shield Advanced** adds 24/7 Shield Response Team, cost protection for attack-driven scaling, and automatic L7 mitigation.
**Firewall Manager** pushes WAF, Shield, security group and Network Firewall policies to every account in the organization, including new ones.

keyFacts.text: Lowest rate limit a **rate-based rule** accepts. Evaluation windows are 1, 2, 5 (default) or 10 minutes; a scope-down statement limits it to a path.
WAF Fraud Control managed rules detect credential stuffing on login (ATP) and fake sign-ups (ACFP), even from many IPs.
Managed rule group that labels bots by category and verifies search engines, so scrapers are blocked while Googlebot is allowed.
Shield Advanced **automatic application layer DDoS mitigation** writes and deploys WAF rules during a flood; it needs a web ACL associated.

traps: Plain IP-based rate limiting fails against attacks spread across many IPs; use ATP or Bot Control.
WAF does not attach to an NLB, an internet gateway or EC2 directly.
Shield Standard gives no response team or cost protection; only Advanced does.
Security groups and NACLs can't inspect HTTP content, so they can't stop SQL injection.
